compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

Ranked similar-ticket retrieval needs an index over the store, and none exists. ADR 0122 fixed the architecture but left the index unbuilt.

This story builds it on a tier needing no model provider, no credentials and no network, so retrieval works in every installation. The sibling embedding story is an opt-in ranking upgrade over this same index; the sibling surfacing story consumes its query API; the sibling ADR story records the decision and the p95 measured here.

## Approach

### Ranking

sqlite FTS5 over title and description, bm25 weights title 5.0 / description 1.0 — the configuration ADR 0122 measured as the `fts5` baseline (`evals/similar-tickets/measure.py:389-396`, weights `"0.0, 5.0, 1.0"`). Semantic recall@5 0.823 vs the adopted `vector` candidate's 0.876; it beats `vector` at lexical recall@10 (0.993 vs 0.972, p=0.0000), ADR 0122's reason for not removing it. Query text is title plus the first 200 characters of description, per ADR 0122.

Results cap at 5. ADR 0122's decision is scoped to k=5: at k=10 `vector`'s semantic edge is indistinguishable (p=0.3438) while `fts5`'s lexical edge becomes significant, an operating point at which the evidence favours building nothing. A different count invalidates the comparison and would require re-running `measure.py --paired`.

The query API excludes a caller-supplied ticket id. A create queries with its own new ticket's text, which catch-up will already have indexed, so without an exclusion the caller gets that ticket back as its own top match.

`score` is normalized to the closed interval 0 to 1, 1 most relevant. Raw bm25 is negative and orders lower-is-better, inverting the conventional reading and leaving consumers unable to assert on it meaningfully.

### Persistence and freshness

A sqlite file under `.rebar/cache/similar-tickets/`, mirroring the git-ignored derived cache at `.rebar/cache/plan-review/` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/checkpoints.py:33-37`). `.gitignore:23` ignores `.rebar/*` wholesale, so no ignore change is needed and nothing derived can reach the `tickets` branch.

The index persists a map from ticket directory to its last-indexed dir hash. That map is what makes catch-up cheap and what makes new tickets discoverable; both properties come from the map, not from the hash function.

`compute_dir_hash(ticket_dir, event_filenames)` (`src/rebar/reducer/_cache.py:122`) supplies the per-directory hash only. Scoped to one directory and its event filenames, it cannot detect that a whole new ticket directory appeared — it detects change in a known directory, it does not discover. Catch-up therefore runs two steps:

1. **Enumerate** the live ticket-directory set from the store.
2. **Diff** it against the persisted map. No entry means new, so index it. A differing hash means changed, so re-index it. A missing directory means gone, so drop the entry.

Step 1 is what makes a ticket created moments earlier discoverable by the next query; without it catch-up would only re-hash directories it already knew, and a new ticket would never be indexed.

Catch-up is synchronous, in the read phase before serving a query — no daemon, no background thread, no CI trigger — so behaviour is identical on a fresh clone, under MCP, and where no CI provider exists.

### Warm-path cost

On an unchanged store the diff performs no indexing and no FTS5 writes, because every enumerated directory's hash matches its stored value. Warm cost is one directory enumeration plus one stat per event file: no parse, no tokenization, no write. A criterion asserts no re-indexing occurs on an unchanged store, so this is verified rather than assumed.

### Concurrent writers

Several processes can query one index file at once, so two can both observe a changed hash and race to rebuild. Reconciliation builds into a temporary database in the same directory and replaces the live file with `os.rename`, atomic within a filesystem. A reader opening a corrupt or partial index discards it and rebuilds rather than erroring, so the cache is regenerable and needs no eviction path. Concurrent reconcilers converge because each recomputes the hashes it writes, so a loser's work is redone rather than merged.

### Failure disposition

Every failure path returns an empty result rather than raising, so retrieval can never fail a caller. Each swallowed failure logs at warning level first; without that log a corrupt index degrades retrieval to permanently empty results with no observable symptom, indistinguishable from a store with no similar tickets.

### Ratchets

No new config key. Any ratcheted mechanism introduced carries a `# mechanism-ok:` marker naming this ticket.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A query returns at most 5 results. Checked by: a test over a store with more than 5 matches asserting the length bound.
- [ ] Each result carries `id`, `alias`, `title` and `score`. Checked by: a shape test over one result.
- [ ] Every `score` lies in the closed interval 0 to 1, with the top-ranked result holding the maximum of the returned set. Checked by: a test asserting the range and the ordering.
- [ ] A caller-supplied excluded ticket id never appears in that query's results. Checked by: a test querying with a ticket's own text and id and asserting its absence.
- [ ] Catch-up enumerates the live ticket-directory set, so a ticket directory created after the last build is indexed. Checked by: a test creating a directory, running catch-up, then asserting the ticket is returned.
- [ ] Catch-up drops index entries whose ticket directory no longer exists. Checked by: a test removing a directory and asserting the ticket stops being returned.
- [ ] Catch-up re-indexes a ticket whose dir hash changed. Checked by: a test mutating a ticket then asserting the updated text is matchable.
- [ ] Catch-up performs no re-indexing work on an unchanged store. Checked by: a test asserting the re-indexed count is 0 on a second consecutive run.
- [ ] A warm query completes within a p95 of 500 ms over at least 20 runs against a synthetic store the test generates and asserts to hold at least 10,000 tickets. Checked by: a timing test asserting the store's ticket count before measuring.
- [ ] The cold-catch-up p95 over that same synthetic store is emitted as a numeric figure. Checked by: a test asserting the measurement is produced.
- [ ] A ticket created in-process is returned by the next query in that same process, with no daemon, background thread, MCP server or CI involved. Checked by: an integration test.
- [ ] With every model-provider credential environment variable unset, a query returns a non-empty ranked result. Checked by: an integration test clearing the credential environment.
- [ ] After 100 writes and 100 queries against a test store, the `tickets` branch contains only user event types. Checked by: an integration test asserting the branch's event-type set.
- [ ] A query returns an empty result rather than raising when the index file is absent. Checked by: a test asserting the return value.
- [ ] A corrupt index file is discarded and rebuilt, and a subsequent query returns results. Checked by: a test corrupting the file then querying.
- [ ] A query returns an empty result rather than raising when catch-up raises. Checked by: a test injecting a raising catch-up.
- [ ] Each swallowed failure emits a warning-level log record. Checked by: a test capturing logs across the absent, corrupt and raising cases and asserting a record for each.
- [ ] Two catch-up runs executing concurrently leave the index readable and both tickets indexed. Checked by: a concurrency test running two in parallel then querying for both.
- [ ] Every module added or modified under `src/rebar/` is at most 800 lines. Checked by: the CI module-size gate.
- [ ] `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` exits 0. Checked by: running it.
- [ ] `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` exits 0. Checked by: running it.
